question: Does the existing 1/0.5 status weighting improve near-obstacle direction over equal weights when angular support contains backgrounds, weak returns or gaps?
hypothesis: Status weighting may move a connected-region bearing, but cannot separate depth layers or undo connectivity merging.

primary_metrics.direction_correct: Exact set of emitted region horizontal labels equals the evaluator near-obstacle direction set. UNKNOWN counts incorrect in the full 60-frame denominator; extra far-background directions count incorrect. This probes a new near-obstacle use, not the original all-return support contract.
primary_metrics.false_center: Number of frames emitting CENTER when the evaluator near-obstacle set does not contain CENTER, including CENTER plus other outputs.
primary_metrics.bilateral_merge: Number of bilateral-truth frames where one emitted region contains zone footprints of both near modes. Count even if its bearing is LEFT or RIGHT; missing modes alone are not merges.

diagnostic_accounting: Record available-mode misses, unsupported extra directions, UNKNOWN frames and adjacent-frame label-set changes for dropout. These are audit fields, not extra retention objectives.
retention_rule: Retain status weighting only if it has strictly more exact-correct frames in the pooled near_far_background and same_zone_pole_wall cases, no lower overall exact correctness, and no increase in either primary error count. Otherwise remove it from the default and retain only the reproducibility comparator.
budget: Exactly six fixed families of ten packets; no training, tuning, capture, threshold sweep or automatic successor. Mirrored pairs except one fixed ten-frame dropout sequence.
limits: No physical echo generation, calibrated reliability, actual RGB image, fusion arbitration, natural accuracy or safety evidence. No-return physical truth is evaluator-only and must not be recovered by invention. CPU scalar metadata workload: TASK_NOT_GPU_SUITABLE.
